parsed.refutation_attempt: No checks on the value of N were found. The value from argv[1] is directly assigned to an int variable without validation. The multiplication N*N is performed in signed 32‑bit arithmetic and is subsequently used to allocate shared memory and to index matrices. Since atoi accepts any integer string, an attacker can supply a value larger than 46340, causing the signed multiplication to overflow (e.g. N=46341). This overflow produces an incorrect size for the shared memory (huge unsigned value after cast to size_t) and leads to potential denial‑of‑service or memory corruption. No defensive checks or constant arguments mitigate this path, and the code path is reachable from user input. Therefore the vulnerability is confirmed.
